title: MSSQL ERROR: setFirstResult and setMaxResults. with string ID
body:
Im using for pagination this query builder for SQL Server:
```javascript
try {
  let posts = await postRepository
                .createQueryBuilder("post")
                .where("post.deletedAt IS NULL")
                .setFirstResult(5)
                .setMaxResults(10)
                .getMany();
  reply(JSON.stringify(posts)).code(200).type('application/json')
} catch (err) {
  reply(JSON.stringify(err)).code(500).type('application/json');
}
```
And I get and error of:
```json
{
  "name": "RequestError",
  "message": "Invalid usage of the option NEXT in the FETCH statement.",
  "code": "EREQUEST",
  "number": 153,
  "lineNumber": 1,
  "state": 2,
  "class": 15,
  "serverName": "SQLServer",
  "procName": "",
  "precedingErrors": [
    {
      "name": "RequestError",
      "message": "Incorrect syntax near 'OFFSET'.",
      "code": "EREQUEST",
      "number": 102,
      "lineNumber": 1,
      "state": 1,
      "class": 15,
      "serverName": "SQLServer",
      "procName": ""
    }
  ]
}
```
For that it seem's to be that SQL Server version 2008 don't support at 
[Invalid usage of the option NEXT in the FETCH statement](http://stackoverflow.com/a/19617772/2116209)

then I try to use limit and offset:
```javascript
try {
  let posts = await postRepository
                .createQueryBuilder("post")
                .where("post.deletedAt IS NULL")
                .offset(5)
                .limit(10)
                .getMany();
  reply(JSON.stringify(posts)).code(200).type('application/json')
} catch (err) {
  reply(JSON.stringify(err)).code(500).type('application/json');
}
```
I get 500 a Internal Server Error without a message.
the  best approach should be updating the mssql?

finally I update to mssql 2016 and found that if you use a primary key type string in this query:
```javascript
let post = await postRepository
                .createQueryBuilder("p")
                .setFirstResult(0)
                .setMaxResults(10)
                .getMany();
```
It will give you a error in the query generated in:
```sql
// this works fine
executing query: 
SELECT DISTINCT("distinctAlias"."u_stringID") as ids_entity 
FROM (
SELECT "u"."stringID" AS "u_stringID",  "u"."name" AS "u_name", "u"."createdAt" AS "u_createdAt", "u"."updatedAt" AS "u_updatedAt", "u"."deletedAt" AS "u_deletedAt" 
FROM "entity" "u") "distinctAlias" 
ORDER BY "ids_entity" 
OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY
// this fails because strindID# treats as number without '' quotes
[0] executing query:
 SELECT "u"."stringID" AS "u_stringID", "u"."name" AS "u_name", "u"."createdAt" AS "u_createdAt", "u"."updatedAt" AS "u_updatedAt", "u"."deletedAt" AS "u_deletedAt" 
FROM "entity" "u" 
WHERE "u"."stringID" 
IN (stringID1, stringID2, stringID3, stringID4, stringID5, stringID6, stringID7, stringID8, stringID9, stringID10 )
```
It seems it fails because treats as a number, without quotes.
but in my entity class a declare as:
```typescript
@PrimaryColumn('string', {length:'32'})
    stringID: string;
```
